newsitem.title: UK: Bagri says peerage honours LME, UK Asians.
newsitem.headline: Bagri says peerage honours LME, UK Asians.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) chairman Raj Bagri said his peerage on Tuesday was recognition both of the world role of the exchange and of the way that people of Asian origin had contributed to the UK economy. Bagri, 66, was made a life peer in Queen Elizabeth's New Year's Honours List. He said by telephone from Bali where he is on holiday, "I am absolutely delighted. I accept this honour with great humility.

"I am happy that, notwithstanding the Sumitomo affair, the position of the LME as the world's largest metals market is recognized through me as its chairman. "...the world will see this recognition as a symbol that the British government takes us seriously in the way that we take seriously our obligations to the international trade and industry."
Bagri's peerage comes against the background of the LME's most turbulent year since the 1985 collapse of the tin price, with the market rocked by the Sumitomo Corp scandal in June.

The Japanese metals conglomerate fired its head copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he had admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading. Bagri said the honour recognised "the contribution which is being made by people of Asian origin to the economic life of the United Kingdom."

Born in Calcutta where he started work as a filing clerk in a metals business in 1945, Bagri now owns and runs the multinational Metdist Group of companies with annual turnover of around 500 million sterling.
"I am very proud of my origin," Bagri said.
